text:
Alex: pasted a tool call and got a 400: "invalid_tool_args: parse error: unexpected token `"
Alex: here's what I sent:
```json
{"tool": "fetch_invoice", "args": {"invoice_id": "inv_12345", "note": "see template: `Hello ${user}`",},}
```
Morgan: I tried to repro locally, parser fails right after the backtick. also noticed trailing comma in args block.
Sasha: two things to check: (1) trailing commas — many strict JSON parsers choke on them; (2) the backtick + ${...} came from a pasted template, but backticks are valid inside JSON strings. error wording pointing at `makes me think shell quoting mangled it.
Morgan: client reported they used a shell heredoc with $'...' quoting around payload when calling curl. that could expand escapes.
Alex: original paste came from a Markdown code block in a docs page with inline template placeholders. I copy/pasted the snippet into terminal.
support-bot: created ticket SUP-2345 and tagged eng-oncall 
eng-oncall: can you share the exact curl command you ran and the SDK/version? also paste raw bytes if possible.
Alex: repro curl below:
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/call \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer xxxxx' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d $'{"tool":"fetch_invoice","args":{"invoice_id":"inv_12345","note":"see template: `Hello ${user}`",},}'
```
eng-oncall: found the issue — the $'...' shell quoting causes the shell to interpret backslashes/escapes and can produce control characters; combined with the trailing comma this yields a parser error that points at the backtick. also some shells will strip or re-encode backticks in odd ways.
eng-oncall: recommended fixes: use --data-binary @payload.json or pass a properly escaped JSON string without $'...' quoting; remove trailing commas from JSON; or wrap payload in single quotes without $ if you don't need escape expansion.
Alex: switched to --data-binary @payload.json and removed trailing commas — request accepted. thanks!
support-bot: SUP-2345 marked resolved :white_check_mark:
